just_in.title: New Jersey Purges 6,600 Noncitizens From Voter Rolls After DMV Software Error
just_in.excerpt: Governor Mikie Sherrill says a glitch in the state's motor vehicle system automatically registered noncitizens to vote between 2023 and 2024, with nearly 400 casting ballots in past elections.
just_in.image_caption: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill at an official event. Sherrill announced the removal of 6,600 noncitizens from the state's voter rolls after a motor vehicle system software error.
just_in.nri_angle: The incident raises questions for Indian Americans and other immigrant communities about how automatic voter registration systems interact with noncitizen driver's license programs across 23 states.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Inhaling CO2 Cleared Alzheimer's Proteins in Early Human Trial
just_in.excerpt: A 30-minute session of intermittent high-dose carbon dioxide inhalation flushed toxic proteins from the brain by mimicking deep-sleep cleansing mechanisms, while a separate copper-based drug showed similar promise in mice.
just_in.image_caption: An MRI brain scan displayed on a computer screen in a clinical setting. Researchers presented new findings on clearing Alzheimer's-linked proteins at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference in London.
just_in.nri_angle: India has an estimated 8.8 million people living with dementia, and the findings on accessible treatments like CO2 inhalation could prove especially relevant for diaspora families managing elder care across borders.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Women With PCOS Face Four Times Higher Risk of Heart Disease, Lancet Study Finds
just_in.excerpt: A major US study of more than 413,000 women found those with the recently renamed condition had a fourfold increase in cardiovascular disease risk, even after accounting for obesity and diabetes.
just_in.image_caption: A doctor measures a patient's blood pressure during a clinical consultation. A new Lancet study has found women with PCOS, now renamed PMOS, face four times the risk of heart disease.
just_in.nri_angle: PCOS prevalence in India ranges from 7% to 20%, and South Asian women face elevated baseline cardiovascular risk, making the study's findings of compounding heart disease risk especially relevant for the diaspora.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Spain's World Cup Win Reshuffles 2026 Ballon d'Or Race
just_in.excerpt: Rodri's Golden Ball, Mbappé's record-breaking Golden Boot, and Messi's final heartbreak have scrambled a wide-open field before voting begins in September.
just_in.image_caption: Spain midfielder Rodri during the 2026 World Cup semifinal against France. He was named the tournament's best player and is now a leading contender for his second Ballon d'Or.
just_in.nri_angle: Messi's massive following in India and the diaspora's growing football engagement make the Ballon d'Or race a closely watched conversation across the subcontinent.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Disney Cuts Hundreds of Jobs With Pixar Bearing the Brunt
just_in.excerpt: Pixar Animation Studios faces the deepest cuts in Disney's third round of layoffs under CEO Josh D'Amaro, even as the studio rides a $1.2 billion box office year.
just_in.image_caption: Pixar Animation Studios headquarters in Emeryville, California. The studio is facing its largest round of layoffs since 2024 as parent company Disney restructures under CEO Josh D'Amaro.
just_in.nri_angle: Indian-origin animation and VFX professionals in Hollywood face heightened job insecurity as successive studio layoffs tighten available positions for workers on employer-sponsored visas.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: InMobi Taps JPMorgan and Jefferies for $1 Billion India IPO
just_in.excerpt: India's first unicorn has appointed four investment banks to manage its upcoming public offering, seeking a valuation of up to $6 billion as it re-domiciles from Singapore.
just_in.image_caption: InMobi CEO Naveen Tewari, who holds about 40% of the company. The Harvard-educated founder is steering India's first unicorn toward a landmark domestic IPO.
just_in.nri_angle: InMobi's listing offers diaspora investors a rare chance to access India's first unicorn through public markets, amid a broader wave of tech IPOs reshaping the country's digital economy.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: MTR Foods Bets on Quick Commerce, Clean Labels and a Viral Sambar Anthem
just_in.excerpt: The 102-year-old Karnataka brand is pairing heritage marketing with digital distribution to expand nationally, while a folk-fusion 'Sambar Anthem' racks up nearly 8 million YouTube views.
just_in.image_caption: A pot of vegetable sambar, the South Indian lentil dish at the heart of MTR's latest marketing campaign. The 102-year-old brand's viral 'Sambar Anthem' has drawn nearly 8 million YouTube views since launching in early July.
just_in.nri_angle: Quick commerce platforms are making MTR's South Indian products accessible to consumers nationwide, including diaspora communities who moved away from the South and seek authentic regional food on demand.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: India U-19 Dominate Sri Lanka After Dramatic Collapse Recovery in Youth Test
just_in.excerpt: Kushagra Ojha's 111 and Manal Chauhan's stunning 150 powered India from 0/2 to 411 all out, before bowlers reduced Sri Lanka to 122/8 by stumps on Day 2 of the 2nd Youth Test in Colombo.
just_in.image_caption: Kushagra Ojha poses after reaching his century during the 2nd Youth Test against Sri Lanka in Colombo. The 16-year-old from Rajasthan scored 111 to rescue India from a 0/2 collapse on the opening day.
just_in.nri_angle: India's youth cricket pipeline continues to produce future stars, with 16-year-old Kushagra Ojha from Rajasthan and Anvay Dravid among the emerging talents the diaspora can follow.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Rahul Gandhi Detained Outside Modi's Home Amid India Exam Protest
just_in.excerpt: Delhi police detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi, his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, and other opposition figures during a sit-in protest demanding the resignation of PM Modi and Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over exam leaks and a crackdown on student demonstrators.
just_in.image_caption: Rahul Gandhi sits on the road outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi's residence as police attempt to remove him during Tuesday's protest. The Congress leader was demanding answers over police action against student demonstrators and the resignation of the education minister.
just_in.nri_angle: The political crisis over exam integrity and youth unemployment resonates directly with Indian diaspora families weighing educational pathways and career prospects for children in India.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Japan Protests China's Live-Fire Naval Drill in Disputed Pacific Waters
just_in.excerpt: Tokyo lodges formal diplomatic protest after a Chinese guided-missile destroyer conducted a live-fire exercise near Japan's southernmost atoll, marking the first such public disclosure of Chinese military drills in Japan's exclusive economic zone.
just_in.nri_angle: The incident reinforces shared India-Japan security concerns in the Indo-Pacific, with both nations deepening Quad and bilateral defense cooperation to counter Chinese naval assertiveness.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Indian Professionals Turn to EB-5 Investor Visas as Green Card Waits Stretch Decades
just_in.excerpt: With EB-2 wait times exceeding 40 years and H-1B policy uncertainty mounting, a 25-fold surge in Indian EB-5 filings is reshaping the US immigration landscape.
just_in.image_caption: The exterior of a US Immigration and Customs Enforcement building. Indian EB-5 investor visa filings have surged 25-fold since 2022 as green card backlogs stretch decades for skilled professionals.
just_in.nri_angle: Indian-American professionals on H-1B visas face 40-60 year green card waits, pushing thousands to invest $800,000+ in EB-5 as an alternative pathway to permanent residency before a September 2026 deadline.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Allahabad HC Splits on Bulldozer Ban, Slams India's 'Normalised Corruption'
just_in.excerpt: Justice Atul Sreedharan proposed a two-year ban on demolishing homes of accused persons, citing the Ram Temple donation theft as the 'nadir of Indian integrity,' but co-judge Justice Siddharth Nandan called the restrictions 'unwarranted judicial activism.'
just_in.image_caption: The Allahabad High Court building in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. A division bench of the court delivered a split verdict on Monday over the legality of demolishing homes of accused persons.
just_in.nri_angle: The ruling raises fundamental questions about rule of law and executive overreach in India, issues closely watched by the Indian diaspora concerned about civil liberties and institutional integrity.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: La Liga Chief Tebas Calls on FIFA's Infantino to Resign Over World Cup Overreach
just_in.excerpt: Spain's top football administrator accuses FIFA of 'destroying the football industry' through relentless tournament expansion and political interference, joining a growing chorus demanding change at the governing body.
just_in.image_caption: La Liga president Javier Tebas at a press event in 2024. Tebas has called on FIFA president Gianni Infantino to resign, accusing the governing body of destroying the football industry through tournament expansion.
just_in.nri_angle: India's AIFF holds a vote in FIFA's 2027 presidential election, and the federation's stance on governance reform and tournament expansion could shape whether FIFA prioritizes grassroots development in emerging markets.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

just_in.title: Trump Booed, Mocked by Stewart After Crashing World Cup Trophy Ceremony
just_in.excerpt: The U.S. president drew loud jeers at MetLife Stadium and refused to leave the stage as Spain celebrated their second World Cup title, prompting a blistering response from The Daily Show host.
just_in.image_caption: Fans fill a packed soccer stadium under bright lights during a night match. President Trump was booed loudly by the MetLife Stadium crowd during the 2026 World Cup final trophy ceremony on Sunday.
just_in.nri_angle: The political spectacle at the World Cup final resonated with the Indian diaspora's deep engagement with both American politics and global football, particularly as India's growing fan base watched the tournament closely.

news.excerpt: A 20-year-old woman was left permanently disabled when groomsmen tossed her in a bedsheet during a traditional hazing ritual, reigniting debate over dangerous wedding customs across Asia.
news.nri_angle: The case highlights risks of dangerous wedding traditions, a concern that resonates with Indian communities where elaborate wedding rituals can sometimes lead to accidents.

news.excerpt: The Cockroach Janta Party removed Dahiya from all official duties after he dismissed accountability to protesters, calling their criticism "nonsense."
news.nri_angle: The CJP movement has resonated with Indians abroad who have staged solidarity protests in London and other cities over the NEET paper leak scandal.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Fourth Person Dies in New York City's Legionnaires' Disease Outbreak
news.excerpt: The death toll from a Legionnaires' disease cluster on Manhattan's Upper East Side has risen to four, with 76 cases reported, though health officials say the source of the outbreak has been eliminated.
news.image_caption: Buildings on the Manhattan skyline. Health officials ordered 76 buildings with cooling towers in the affected Upper East Side zip codes to undergo emergency disinfection.
news.nri_angle: New York City is home to one of the largest Indian diaspora communities in the United States, with significant populations in the affected Upper East Side neighborhoods. South Asian residents and workers in the area should monitor for flu-like symptoms.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: UK's New PM Burnham Scraps VAT on Electricity Bills in First Policy Move
news.excerpt: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the removal of value-added tax from domestic electricity bills starting October 1, saving households around £45 a year in his first major policy action.
news.image_caption: Andy Burnham at 10 Downing Street. The 56-year-old former Mayor of Greater Manchester became Britain's Prime Minister on Monday after Keir Starmer stepped down.
news.nri_angle: The UK is home to 1.8 million people of Indian origin, making it one of the largest NRI communities in the world. Rising energy costs have been a persistent concern for Indian families in Britain, particularly those running small businesses or supporting multi-generational households. The VAT cut will directly reduce their electricity bills from October.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: US Mercenary Wins Food Relief in Delhi's Tihar Jail After Hunger Strike
news.excerpt: A Delhi court allowed American national Matthew Aaron VanDyke, charged under India's anti-terror laws, to receive food of his choice in Tihar Jail after a prolonged hunger strike left him 14 kg lighter.
news.nri_angle: VanDyke's case highlights the intersection of international security and Indian anti-terror law enforcement, with implications for foreign nationals detained in India.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: US Missile Stockpiles Hit Critical Lows as Iran War Drags On
news.excerpt: Analysts warn America has burned through up to 61% of its Patriot missiles and 80% of THAAD interceptors, raising questions about the Pentagon’s ability to sustain prolonged operations — and its readiness for threats elsewhere.
news.nri_angle: US munitions depletion could delay defense deliveries to India and push New Delhi to accelerate indigenous manufacturing under Atmanirbhar Bharat.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Schumer Pushes Bill to Break Up Meatpacking Giants and Lower Grocery Prices
news.excerpt: The Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act would force Tyson, JBS, Cargill, and National Beef to choose a single protein line, targeting an industry where four companies control 85% of U.S. beef processing.
news.image_caption: U.S. Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer is pushing legislation to break up major meatpacking companies and lower grocery prices for consumers.
news.nri_angle: Chicken is a staple protein in many South Asian households, and any restructuring of the meatpacking industry could affect poultry prices. Greater competition could also benefit independent ethnic grocery retailers.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: IIT Roorkee Backtracks on Advisory Warning Students Against Political Movements
news.excerpt: After social media backlash, the premier engineering institute clarified that an internal email asking students not to 'show affinity to political movements' was an annual advisory, not a new directive issued amid the ongoing CJP protests.
news.image_caption: The main building of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee. The institution retracted an advisory that had warned students against participating in political movements.
news.nri_angle: IIT alumni in Silicon Valley and global academia face questions about academic freedom at India's elite institutions amid exam system credibility crisis
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Bengaluru Triple Murder Accused Used AI Chatbot for Six Months to Plan Killings
news.excerpt: Police say Kenneth, 25, consulted an AI chatbot about killing methods, body disposal, and evidence removal before the June stabbing of his partner's parents and sister. Investigators have now written to the AI company seeking his full chat history.
news.image_caption: A laptop displays an AI chatbot interface. Bengaluru police say the accused in a triple murder case used an AI chatbot for six months to plan the killings and research methods of evidence disposal.
news.nri_angle: The case raises concerns about AI safety guardrails globally, adding to a pattern of chatbot-linked violent crimes that includes the USF student killings in Florida.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Pentagon Faces Funding Crisis as Iran War Costs Spiral Beyond $29 Billion
news.excerpt: The Defense Department is burning through cash faster than expected, but key Republicans are balking at a $95 billion emergency spending package, demanding more transparency on war costs and strategy before signing off.
news.image_caption: The Pentagon, headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense, in Arlington, Virginia. The building houses the sprawling bureaucracy now scrambling to secure tens of billions in emergency war funding from a skeptical Congress.
news.nri_angle: Strait of Hormuz disruptions impact India energy imports and Gulf-based Indian workers; Indian government watching conflict impact on diaspora in targeted Gulf states
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Two Indian Men Jailed in Singapore After Swapping $235,000 Diamond With Fake Stone at Chinatown Jeweller
news.excerpt: The pair posed as customers, replaced the diamond with a counterfeit during inspection, and were arrested at Changi Airport hours later while trying to flee the country.
news.image_caption: A diamond displayed in a jewellery store setting. Two Indian men were arrested in Singapore for swapping a S$235,000 diamond with a fake stone at a Chinatown shop.
news.nri_angle: The case is the latest in a series of theft arrests involving Indian nationals in Singapore, raising concerns about stereotyping within the Indian community abroad.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Lakhs March to Parliament Over NEET Paper Leak as Sonam Wangchuk's Hunger Strike Enters Day 23
news.excerpt: Tens of thousands of protesters clashed with police in New Delhi on the opening day of Parliament's monsoon session, demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over India's worst exam scandal in years.
news.image_caption: Sonam Wangchuk, the Ladakh-based activist whose 23-day hunger strike has become the focal point of India's anti-paper-leak movement. Wangchuk was forcibly moved to Safdarjung Hospital on July 18 after losing about 9 kg during his fast.
news.nri_angle: The crisis deepens skepticism among diaspora families about India's national testing infrastructure, especially those with children aspiring to medical seats back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Quad Unveils Fiji Port Project and Critical Minerals Pact at New Delhi Meeting
news.excerpt: Foreign ministers from India, the U.S., Japan, and Australia announced the Quad's first joint infrastructure project and new frameworks for critical minerals, energy security, and maritime surveillance at their May 26 meeting in New Delhi.
news.image_caption: India's External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who chaired the Quad Foreign Ministers' Meeting in New Delhi on May 26. The ministers announced the grouping's first joint infrastructure project in Fiji and new pacts on critical minerals and energy security.
news.nri_angle: The Quad's critical minerals framework and Pax Silica semiconductor initiative could accelerate foreign investment in India's technology manufacturing sector, creating new opportunities for Indian professionals in diversified global supply chains.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Sikkim Tunnel Death Toll Rises to Ten as Rescuers Battle Gas and Debris
news.excerpt: Ten bodies recovered from the collapsed ADIT-3 tunnel at NHPC's Teesta Stage VI hydroelectric project in Namchi district, with more than 15 workers still feared trapped inside the gas-filled passage.
news.image_caption: Police personnel at the site of the collapsed tunnel in Sikkim's Namchi district as rescue operations continue on Tuesday. At least ten workers have been killed and more than 15 remain trapped inside the NHPC hydroelectric project tunnel following a suspected gas explosion.
news.nri_angle: The victims hailed from migrant-worker communities in West Bengal, Assam, Punjab, and Uttarakhand, underscoring the human cost borne by India's mobile labour force in hazardous Himalayan construction.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Declares Indus Treaty 'Cannot Function,' Plans 5,500 MW of New J&K Hydro Projects
news.excerpt: New Delhi hardens its stance on the suspended water-sharing agreement with Pakistan, fast-tracking major dam projects on the Chenab and Jhelum rivers.
news.image_caption: The Baglihar Dam on the Chenab River in Jammu & Kashmir. India has fast-tracked several hydropower projects on the Chenab and Jhelum rivers after suspending the Indus Waters Treaty.
news.nri_angle: For diaspora members with roots in J&K, the hydropower push promises long-delayed economic development in a region historically constrained by treaty restrictions.

nri-world.title: CJP's 'Chalo Sansad' March Draws Thousands as Protest Movement Goes Global
nri-world.excerpt: The youth-led Cockroach Janta Party staged its boldest action yet with a march toward Parliament on the first day of the monsoon session, while Indian students abroad amplified calls for the education minister's resignation.
nri-world.image_caption: Youth-led protests at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi have drawn students, activists and parents from across India demanding accountability over examination irregularities. The CJP movement has also gained traction among Indian communities overseas.
nri-world.nri_angle: The CJP movement has deep diaspora roots — founder Abhijeet Dipke is a Boston University student who flew from the US to lead the protests. Indian students in London confronted Chief Justice Surya Kant at a Birkbeck College event, while solidarity campaigns have spread across diaspora social media.

nri-world.title: Supreme Court Removes Government Supervision Over Kerala Waqf Board
nri-world.excerpt: The apex court deleted the Kerala High Court's direction placing the Waqf Board under a Joint Secretary's administration, though restrictions on major decisions remain amid an ongoing challenge to the Board's composition.
nri-world.image_caption: The Supreme Court of India. The court has removed government supervision over the Kerala Waqf Board in a significant ruling on religious board governance.
nri-world.nri_angle: The Waqf Amendment Act dispute has directly affected Indian diaspora communities closely following the Munambam land case and broader questions of religious property governance and minority rights in India.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Delhi High Court Allows Sonam Wangchuk's Transfer to Medanta Hospital
nri-world.excerpt: A Division Bench overturned a single-judge order that had refused the climate activist's transfer from Safdarjung Hospital, with government raising no objection to the move.
nri-world.image_caption: Sonam Wangchuk, the Ladakhi climate activist and education reformer, in a 2017 photograph. The Delhi High Court on Tuesday ordered his transfer from Safdarjung Hospital to Medanta Hospital after a legal battle over his medical care during a 24-day hunger strike.
nri-world.nri_angle: Wangchuk is internationally recognized for his ice stupa innovation and as the inspiration behind the Bollywood film 3 Idiots; his fast has drawn global attention to India's exam-reform movement.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Miami's Cost of Living Surpasses New York City's for the First Time
nri-world.excerpt: Federal data shows the Miami metro area is now America's second most expensive region after San Francisco, as soaring insurance premiums, property taxes, and post-pandemic inflation erode Florida's no-income-tax advantage.
nri-world.image_caption: YouTube / Roque Castro - Living in Miami Florida
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian American professionals who relocated to South Florida during the pandemic for tax savings now face an all-in cost of living that may erode those benefits.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian Diaspora Protests Outside India House in London Over NEET Controversy and Delhi Crackdown
nri-world.excerpt: Demonstrators demanded Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation over the NEET examination scandal and voiced solidarity with climate activist Sonam Wangchuk.
nri-world.image_caption: Protesters gathered outside a government building. Indian diaspora members demonstrated outside India House in London over the NEET exam controversy.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian diaspora in the UK directly involved in political protest over domestic Indian issues, reflecting a growing trend of transnational activism.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Mamata Rallies INDIA Bloc for Unity as TMC Split Deepens Ahead of Monsoon Session
nri-world.excerpt: Despite losing 20 MPs to a rebel faction and three Rajya Sabha members to the BJP, Mamata Banerjee is pushing opposition parties to close ranks against the ruling alliance as Parliament's monsoon session begins.
nri-world.image_caption: Mamata Banerjee, founder-chairperson of the Trinamool Congress, photographed in Kolkata. Banerjee is pushing for opposition unity through the INDIA bloc even as her party faces its deepest internal crisis since 1998.
nri-world.nri_angle: The TMC split and opposition realignment hold political and cultural significance for West Bengal's large diaspora community, shaping conversations about governance and democratic accountability in India.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Wins Two Golds and Four Silvers at International Mathematical Olympiad, Finishes Seventh Globally
nri-world.excerpt: A six-member Indian team delivered the country's fourth consecutive top-10 finish at the world's most prestigious maths competition, held in Shanghai with a record 680 participants from 117 nations.
nri-world.image_caption: The International Mathematical Olympiad logo represents the world's oldest and most prestigious mathematics competition for pre-university students. The 67th edition was held in Shanghai, China, with a record 680 participants from 117 countries.
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian students competing and excelling internationally in STEM reflects the diaspora's emphasis on academic achievement and inspires NRI families worldwide.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Satchin Panda Resigns From Salk Institute After Sexual Misconduct Allegations
nri-world.excerpt: Indian-origin circadian biology researcher leaves prestigious California institute after 22 years following workplace misconduct investigation
nri-world.image_caption: The Salk Institute for Biological Studies in La Jolla, California. Indian-origin circadian biology researcher Satchin Panda resigned from the institute amid sexual misconduct allegations.
nri-world.nri_angle: The resignation of a celebrated Indian-origin scientist raises questions about accountability in elite Western research institutions where many diaspora members build their careers.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Bihar-Born Kanishka Narayan Becomes UK's First Minister for Artificial Intelligence
nri-world.excerpt: The 36-year-old Labour MP, who moved from Muzaffarpur to Cardiff at age 12, has been elevated to a newly created cabinet-level AI role under Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
nri-world.image_caption: Kanishka Narayan in his official UK Parliament portrait. The Bihar-born MP was appointed as the UK's first Minister for Artificial Intelligence on July 20, 2026.
nri-world.image_credit: UK Parliament, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin MP from Bihar elevated to UK's first cabinet-level AI minister, representing growing Indian political influence in Western democracies.
